input: The disagreement over the benchmark material is, on closer inspection, narrower than the two sets of values might initially suggest. One of the groups tested the material as a loose powder, whereas the other tested formed pellets held in a shallow holder, and the second set of values includes the resistance of the holder itself, which the authors leave incorporated within the reported drop. The powder bed is also finer and considerably more closely packed than the formed body that the duty will actually contain, so that the two tests are in reality measuring different packings, rather than measuring one and the same packing at two different levels of care. The loadings stated by the pellet group lie closer to the working loading of the separation in question, and its gas rates have the additional merit of covering the range that the duty requires. IAST underlies the calculations of both groups and can therefore account for none of the difference that separates them. The pellet values are accordingly to be preferred, although on that condition alone: that is to say, formed material, loadings close to the working loading, and rates within the range that the duty requires. Outside those particular conditions, the preference lapses altogether, and a fresh measurement carried out on the material in its formed state is the only remedy that either group has to offer.
target: The disagreement over the benchmark material is narrower than the two sets of values suggest. One group tested loose powder; the other tested formed pellets in a shallow holder, and the second set of values includes the resistance of the holder, which the authors leave in the reported drop. The powder bed is also finer and more closely packed than the formed body the duty will contain, so the two tests measure different packings, not one packing measured at two levels of care. The conditions each group chose were reasonable for the question each was asking; the difficulty is that the design question is only one of them. The pellet group's stated loadings lie closer to the working loading of the separation, and its gas rates cover the range the duty needs. IAST underlies both groups' calculations and accounts for none of the difference. The pellet values are preferred, on that condition alone: formed material, loadings near the working loading, rates within the range the duty requires. Outside those conditions the preference lapses, and a fresh measurement on the material as formed is the only remedy either group offers.
